hdi.source: Karnataka State Human Development Report 2022 (Dept. of Planning, Programme Monitoring & Statistics)

keySectors: Thermal power generation — RTPS (1,720 MW) and YTPS (1,600 MW), ~3,320 MW total in-district capacity
Gold mining — Hutti Gold Mines Company Ltd (HGML), Lingasugur taluk
Paddy cultivation and rice milling (Tungabhadra/Krishna canal command)
Groundnut, bengal gram, jowar, bajra and sunflower
Chilli — the district's MoFPI 'One District One Product' selection
Agricultural education and research (University of Agricultural Sciences, Raichur)
strengths: Major power hub: Raichur Thermal Power Station (1,720 MW — 7x210 MW plus 1x250 MW, KPCL, at Shaktinagar) and Yermarus Thermal Power Station (1,600 MW — 2x800 MW supercritical, Raichur Power Corporation Ltd, dedicated 2018) give the district roughly 3,320 MW of installed capacity

Hutti Gold Mines Company Ltd — one of India's few operating gold producers: 1,691.50 kg of gold, Rs 1,910.62 Cr revenue and Rs 844.71 Cr profit after tax in FY 2025-26, with ore capacity raised to about 3,000 tonnes/day
Ranked 1st among 115 NITI Aayog Aspirational Districts in the June 2023 delta ranking, qualifying for a Rs 10 Cr award; had earlier ranked first on agriculture & water resources
Large irrigated command area: Tungabhadra Left Bank Canal design CCA of 323,744 ha (shared with Koppal) plus Narayanapura Right Bank Canal irrigating 84,000 ha in Lingasugur and Devadurga taluks
Paddy is the district's largest crop by area (~254,363 ha targeted in 2023-24) with high productivity (~4,900 kg/ha), supporting a substantial rice milling industry
Officially styled the 'Cotton Bowl of Karnataka' — cotton area ~153,096 ha targeted in 2023-24
Rice milling cluster: Invest Karnataka cites over 100 rice mills; the Raichur Rice Mills Association claims more than 150 major/medium mills
Balanced sex ratio of 1000 females per 1000 males (Census 2011), unusual for a low-income district
University of Agricultural Sciences, Raichur (established 2009) anchors agricultural R&D for the Kalyana Karnataka region
Eight KIADB-listed industrial areas (Raichur IA, Deosugur IA, Raichur Growth Centre, Yermarus IA, Manvi IA, Devadurga IA plus two private estates)
Raichur upgraded from City Municipal Council to City Corporation in 2024
Greenfield airport received MoEFCC environmental clearance in April 2025 (Rs 2.08 billion, 0.15 million passengers per annum design capacity)
challenges: Per capita income of Rs 1,67,810 (2023-24) is roughly half the Karnataka average of Rs 3,39,813
HDI 0.562, ranked 28th of 30 Karnataka districts — part of the bottom cluster with Kalaburagi (0.539) and Yadgir (0.538)
The mean-years-of-schooling index is 0.175, by far the weakest component of the district's HDI and a severe education-stock deficit
Female literacy of 48.73% versus male 70.47% — a 21.7 percentage-point gender gap (Census 2011)
Overall literacy 59.56%, far below the Karnataka average of 75.36%; rural literacy is only 54.11%
Groundwater constrained and contaminated — fluoride and salinity problems documented by the WellLabs Raichur Transformation Lab, alongside waterlogging and soil salinisation in canal areas
Repeated droughts since 2012-13 driving agrarian distress and large-scale distress out-migration
Inequitable canal water distribution between head-reach and tail-end farmers in the Tungabhadra command
Raichur city receives about 52 MLD of water against demand of roughly 90 MLD for a city population near 3.5 lakh
No AIIMS has been sanctioned for Raichur despite a long-running public demand; the Centre has repeatedly deferred it
Karnataka's approved PM MITRA mega textile park went to Kalaburagi, not Raichur, despite Raichur's cotton base
No single authoritative district irrigation-coverage figure exists — published estimates range from 20% of geographical area to ~36% of net sown area depending on denominator
opportunities: Move cotton up the value chain — ginning is present but spinning, yarn and apparel are largely absent despite the district's raw cotton base
Chilli processing and value addition, backed by the district's MoFPI One District One Product selection (green chilli: ~3,092 ha and ~37,844 t in 2023-24)
Rice milling modernisation and by-product use (bran oil, husk-based energy) across the 100+ mill cluster
Red gram / pulse processing — tur area of ~145,890 ha with low productivity (~570 kg/ha) implies large yield-improvement headroom
Leverage the ~3,320 MW power base and existing KIADB estates to attract power-intensive manufacturing
Close the female-literacy and schooling gap — the single highest-leverage intervention on the district's HDI, given the 0.175 mean-years-of-schooling index
Fluoride and salinity remediation plus equitable canal water distribution, building on the Raichur Transformation Lab situation analysis
Convert Aspirational District momentum (rank 1 of 115 in June 2023) into sustained sectoral programmes
Complete the greenfield airport to improve connectivity for the gold, power and agri-processing sectors
Groundnut and sunflower oil extraction — oilseed area exists but processing is limited

dataCompleteness.verificationNote: Demographics, district GDDP/NDDP/PCI, HDI and the major power/mining assets are sourced. Crop figures are official TARGETS, not actuals. Sectoral GDDP composition is a state-average proxy and is likely wrong for this district. No roadmap, investment pipeline, credit, MSME or KPI-target tables are included because no verified district-level figures were available.

removedInThisRevision: 'Sugarcane: 80,000 ha, 25 sugar mills, Rs 1,200 Cr/year, 25,000 TCD capacity' — badly wrong. Raichur's targeted sugarcane area for 2023-24 was 1,234 ha, about 1.5% of the claimed figure. No evidence of 25 sugar mills was found.
'Groundnut: 120,000 ha, 3rd largest in India' — actual targeted area is 47,946 ha and the national-rank claim is unsourced.
'200+ cotton ginning units' — cotton ginning exists but no unit inventory could be sourced.
'Lowest per capita income in Karnataka' and 'lowest HDI in Karnataka (0.501, rank 30/30)' — both false. Raichur's HDI is 0.562, rank 28/30; Yadgir (0.538) is last and Kalaburagi (0.539) is 29th.

roadmap / industries / creditData / msme / investments / kpis / roleDashboards blocks — these contained invented budgets, job counts, mill capacities, progress percentages and credit tables presented with false source attribution. Removed rather than corrected.
correctedInThisRevision: rural: 1,398,203 -> 1,438,464 and urban: 530,609 -> 490,348 (Census 2011 actual; verified against the rural/urban male-female breakdowns)
GDDP: Rs 57,612 Cr (state-GSDP-derived estimate) -> Rs 42,211 Cr (DES district GDDP, 2023-24, current prices)
Per capita income: Rs 2,98,690 (estimate) -> Rs 1,67,810 (DES per capita NDDP, 2023-24). The old figure was ~78% too high and wrongly implied Raichur was near the state average.
gddpComposition: the previously stated 28.5 / 18.2 / 53.3 split was invented; reverted to the state-average proxy with an explicit warning
Added the district's two largest industrial assets — RTPS (1,720 MW) and YTPS (1,600 MW) — and Hutti Gold Mines, none of which appeared in the previous version
